title: Microsoft Teams: customise the file types blocked by Weaponizable File Protection
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout, default behaviour and documented controls are supported. Microsoft does not substantiate the blanket statement that the protection takes no other autonomous action; the licensing wording also understates the published general Teams licence requirement.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let Teams administrators customise which file types Weaponizable File Protection blocks.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to customize which file types are blocked in Teams to align with their organization's security requirements

claims.claim: Administrators can instead continue using Microsoft's recommended default list.
claims.quote: or continue using the Microsoft-recommended default list.

claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and 'Licensing is not yet published' with: 'Teams users need a Microsoft Teams licence, except for joining meetings anonymously. No requirement specific to customising Weaponizable File Protection was found at the time of checking (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Keep the warning not to promise that the feature is free, and narrow the licensing open question and cost rationale to feature-specific requirements.

claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Messaging settings.
3. Scroll down to Messaging safety settings.
4. Turn on the setting: Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCheck Enabled|Disabled -Identity Global switches file protection on or off.
claims.quote:
This setting enables weaponizable file detection in Teams messages in the tenant.
Possible Values:
- Enabled
- Disabled

claims.claim: FileTypeCheck is an existing protection switch, not the setting that chooses blocked extensions.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCheck "Enabled" -Identity Global
The list of blocked file types isn't currently configurable by administrators.
